title: Irregularities & discrepancies flagged for review
method: Anything observed that is inconsistent, stale, impossible, or a structural risk gets a numbered entry here and is never silently normalized. Severity: high = affects trust in a result; medium = affects interpretation; low = cosmetic/monitor.

items.title: Election Assistance Commission has had NO serving commissioners since July 2026
items.detail: Two of three commissioners were dismissed by the president and the remaining one resigned, leaving the federal election-administration commission without a member (Wikipedia, fetched 2026-09-18; Ballotpedia corroborates leadership history). Its guidance output is at risk until reconstituted.
items.action: Treat EAC guidance with caution; no numeric data in this repo depends on it.

items.title: Shared API host returned STALE last_price_dollars / updated_time for CONTROLH-2026
items.detail: On 2026-09-18 the public API on api.elections.kalshi.com showed last_price 0.10 with updated_time 2026-07-14 for CONTROLH-2026-R, while the live web page showed an 89/91 book. The order-book fields (yes_bid/yes_ask) were current. This session's snapshot uses the order-book side and flags the divergence.
items.action: Consumers must prefer yes_bid/yes_ask (or the orderbook endpoint) over last_price_dollars for live markets; re-verified on every collect run.

items.title: covers.com 2026-08-27 guide is internally inconsistent on Senate odds (R 57% in prose, 53% in its own table)
items.detail: The same page's narrative text says Republicans 57% to keep the Senate while its table shows R 53% / D 47%. Unreconciled source data.
items.action: Excluded from the master source list; kept only as a historical cross-check point with both figures recorded.

items.title: Gallup ended presidential approval tracking (Feb 2026) and horse-race election polling (2015)
items.detail: After ~90 years, Gallup no longer polls presidential approval (final measure Dec 2025: 36%) and will not 'publish assessments of individual political figures' (NYT 2026-02-11; CNN 2026-02-12). Any 2026 analysis citing 'Gallup approval' is using stale series.
items.action: Gallup is included as a historical series only; 2026 approval comparisons use CNN Poll of Polls (39%) and Quinnipiac (33%, 2026-09).

items.title: Monmouth University Polling Institute ceased operations 2025-07-01
items.detail: The institute that published the October 2024 generic-ballot polls used in this repo no longer exists (Ballotpedia, fetched 2026-09-18). Its 2024-2025 releases are historical-only.
items.action: Monmouth data used with its cessation noted; no forward reliance.

items.title: FiveThirtyEight website shut down 2025-03-05 (Disney/ABC); archive lives on GitHub
items.detail: 538 the site was dissolved on 2025-03-05 with ~15 layoffs; Silver kept the model IP (now Silver Bulletin). The 2024 polling data used here comes from the GitHub archive, whose final national general-average snapshot is dated 2024-09-12 — there is NO late-October/November 538 series in the public archive.
items.action: The poll-vs-market backtest reuses the 2024-09-12 anchor and reports its age in days per comparison point; late-window poll absence is itself a flagged data gap.

items.title: Hub page percentages can sum to ≠100% (mixed bid/ask display)
items.detail: Examples captured 2026-09-18: MI Secretary of State 95%+14%, KS Attorney General 57%+49%, NH State Senate 75%+30%, MO SD8 80%+31%. The web renders opposite-side quotes from each market's own book, so pairs need not complement.
items.action: This repo stores both the web percentages (as rendered) and, where captured, the raw API bid/ask; consumers should not average web % pairs across markets.

items.title: KXMUSKCHALLENGERS-26: 'At least 3' (13%) priced ABOVE 'At least 1' (12%) — logically impossible
items.detail: The event 'How many Elon-backed challengers will win seats in Congress this year?' shows the 'at least 3' outcome at 13% while 'at least 1' sits at 12%. Since {at least 3} ⊂ {at least 1}, this ordering cannot hold for consistent probabilities. Likely a thin market with a wide/stale book.
items.action: Flagged, not traded in any strategy; monitor for self-correction. If it persists into the 2026 cycle it is a candidate for a market-design anomaly study.

items.title: 34 of 35 Senate seats have tradeable Kalshi markets; Louisiana market is thin; 66 of 435 House districts individually priced
items.detail: predictionmarketspicks.com (2026-09-13) counts 34/35 Senate seats with markets (claims none for LA; the hub does show a thin kxsenatela-26nov — unresolved, recorded both ways) and only 66 competitive House districts with individual markets. The rest are priced only via chamber seat-count and balance-of-power markets.
items.action: The collector script (scripts/collect-kalshi.mjs) enumerates the full live universe every run; thin/missing markets are reported, not imputed.

items.title: Kalshi event contracts: state-vs-CFTC jurisdiction conflict is unresolved
items.detail: CFTC is the exclusive federal regulator (KalshiEX v. CFTC 2024 political-contracts win; CFTC dropped appeal May 2025; Third Circuit 2026-04-06 sports win), but NV/NJ/MD sent cease-and-desist letters and S.D. Ohio (2026-03-09) ruled sports event contracts are NOT swaps in that district. Political contracts (this repo's layer) are the more settled branch, but the regulatory surface is moving.
items.action: Documented; no numeric reliance. Re-checked each session.

items.title: Election-day (2024-11-05) candlestick bar was not captured for the 2024 backtest markets
items.detail: The historical candlestick fetch used end_ts=1730851200 (2024-11-05T00:00Z), so the last captured bar is the Nov 4 trading day (bars end at midnight ET). Settlement outcomes come from the official market objects, so backtest conclusions are unaffected, but the final-day price path is missing from the charts.
items.action: Collectors re-fetch with end_ts = settlement_ts + 86400; until then the site labels the last point as '2024-11-04 (last captured bar)'.

items.title: Poll margin -> win probability uses a logistic mapping (k=4.5) that is a labeled assumption, not a published 538 probability
items.detail: 538's public archive publishes margins, not probabilities. This repo maps margin m to p = 1/(1+exp(-m/4.5)) (the scaling 538 used in its 2020 national model) and labels every use as 'modeled mapping'.
items.action: Sensitivity: at k=3 the same 2024-09-12 anchor (Harris +2.82) implies 31% for Trump instead of 35%; the poll-vs-market gap conclusion is unchanged.

items.title: OpenElections (Harvard Dataverse) site is offline — the openelections.org domain is for sale (fetched 2026-09-19)
items.detail: Fetch of https://www.openelections.org/ on 2026-09-19 returned a GoDaddy 'domain for sale' listing instead of the dataset site. The master list entry 'harvard-dataverse' points to dataverse.harvard.edu, which is live and unaffected; the OpenElections datasets should be reached there (or via the MEDSL dataverse).
items.action: Do not cite openelections.org; use dataverse.harvard.edu datasets with DOIs. Re-check domain status each session.

items.title: U.S. Elections Project (UF) migrated — electproject.org is a stub now pointing to the UF Election Lab (fetched 2026-09-19)
items.detail: electproject.org (Google Sites) states: 'My voter turnout data and analyses have moved to the UF Election Lab (election.lab.ufl.edu/voter-turnout/). All data here supersedes data posted on the old US Elections Project site.'
items.action: Use election.lab.ufl.edu as the canonical VEP-turnout source (master entry 'uf-election-lab'); electproject.org kept for historical pages only.

items.title: Edison Research acquired by SSRS (2025) — edisonresearch.com now redirects to ssrs.com/edison-research-at-ssrs (fetched 2026-09-19)
items.detail: 'In 2025, SSRS acquired Edison Research, gaining nearly three decades of experience measuring audio, media, and consumer behavior, as well as a deep background in election research.' Whether the national exit-poll operation will run at the 2026 midterms under the new ownership is not yet stated on the page.
items.action: Treat 2026 exit-poll sourcing as provisional; confirm the 2026 exit-poll operation and methodology before using exit-poll numbers in any backtest.
